title: Inference health, operational cost & roadmap handoff
summary: Quarterly check-in focused on usage trends, spike investigation from July, cost optimization opportunities (batching, quantization recommendations), Dedicated vs Hosted capacity tradeoffs, and roadmap alignment for next quarter. Agreed on pilot for Dedicated reserved pool sizing and an SLA uplift request. Action items assigned for pricing, security docs, and a short benchmark run with customer sample prompts.
topics: Cost levers: batching, quantization, prefix caching
Roadmap sync: Canary rollouts and eval guardrails
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-08-18 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Maya, Arun, Lila (Redwood); Ravi, Sofia, Derek, Priya (Violet Metrics)

Summary note: conversation has some auto transcription noise; names and acronyms may be slightly off.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got a full agenda, want to start with usage and then go into the July spike. Ravi, do you want to kick us off with how you saw the spike from your side?

[00:28] Ravi Menon: Yeah thanks Maya. So on July 12–14 we saw a 3.8x increase in token throughput for our customer-facing summarization endpoint, most of it midday PST. We traced a chunk to a marketing campaign but some of it looks organic, like a retry loop from mobile devices. We forwarded a log snippet to Lila but we don't have a clear root cause.

[01:05] Lila Gomez: I saw that; we pulled logs on our side and there were a few 5xx bursts. The runtime reported elevated queue lengths — looks like batch formation latency spiked when short requests streamed in concurrently.

[01:40] Arun Patel: Quick note: when batch formation delays you can get higher tail latency that cascades into client retries if retry policies aren't jittered. Also if KV-cache hit rates drop because prefixes differ you'll see more token load.

[02:12] Derek Chu: Our mobile team shipped a small change which dropped prompt templating into a slightly different order, so prefix variance went up; that could drop cache hits.

[02:40] Maya Chen: That aligns. Two immediate things — Lila will share the log correlation spreadsheet and Arun will propose batching and cache config changes. Also we'll run a small benchmark on a sample of your traffic.

[03:15] Sofia Alvarez: On cost, our spend jumped ~42% in July month over month which is unsustainable. We need concrete knobs.

[03:36] Arun Patel: From what we can see, three levers are highest impact: request batching (aggressive continuous batching for ephemeral small prompts), prefix/KV caching (reduce unique prefixes by canonicalization), and quantized model variants for lower-cost paths. We also recommend model selection for the workload — a slightly smaller model with tuned prompts had similar quality in our internal evals.

[04:10] Ravi Menon: How risky is quantization for our use case? We have regulated customers and want to avoid hallucination regressions.

[04:27] Arun Patel: Good question — quantization tends to be safe for deterministic tasks like extractive summarization but we always validate with your eval set. Redwood Optimize can run regressions against a small prompt bank and flag quality delta; we'll include thresholds for rollback.

[05:05] Priya Iyer: On compliance, we need to confirm audit log retention and KMS keys for Dedicated. This was brought up in procurement.

[05:23] Maya Chen: Noted — Lila, can you share the SOC2 / ISO blurb and the Dedicated KMS options?

[05:36] Lila Gomez: Yep — I'll post links after the call. We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and we have audit log exports to S3 or your SIEM. I'll include the security brief and the SOC2 cert snapshot.

[06:02] Sofia Alvarez: Walk me through Dedicated sizing — we want predictable tails and lower 99 latency.

[06:18] Arun Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools. For throughput spikes, we typically advise a baseline pool sized for 95th percentile and an autoscaling buffer for bursts, plus a burst capacity policy. For your July spike, a baseline increase of ~30% with a 2x burst buffer would flatten the tail. We'll show a cost comparison.

[06:48] Derek Chu: Is there a hard SLA uplift if we go Dedicated? Our legal team asked about 99.9 vs 99.5.

[07:00] Maya Chen: We can support SLA tiers on Dedicated with an enterprise addendum. I'll connect you to contracts.

[07:12] Ravi Menon: On the cost spreadsheet you sent, I noticed the embed usage is small but expensive per token — can we move some offline batching to reduce per-call cost?

[07:35] Arun Patel: Yes, for non-real-time flows we recommend async batching to amortize token cost. Also use embeddings compression and caching for repeated queries.

[08:00] Sofia Alvarez: Can you run us a quick back-of-envelope on monthly cost if we: 1) enable continuous batching, 2) move to quantized variant for low-risk routes, 3) reserve a small Dedicated pool for primary traffic?

[08:20] Arun Patel: We can — we'll produce a delta estimate with assumptions and per-token unit economics. Expect 20–35% reduction depending on your traffic mix.

[08:48] Maya Chen: Let's talk reliability incidents. Priya, can you describe the impact on incidents?

[09:00] Priya Iyer: We saw two customer complaints during the spike; the observability alerts were noisy and paging triggered twice. We want better alert tuning and a runbook for degraded KV cache behavior.

[09:22] Lila Gomez: Our Console has route-level error rate and token latency dashboards. We can add a derived alert for rising queue length and low cache hit rate. Also recommend a canary rollout for changes.

[09:45] Ravi Menon: The mobile retry behavior was heavy. I want to reduce client-side retries and rely more on our server-side throttling. Is there a pattern you recommend?

[10:00] Arun Patel: Use exponential backoff with jitter and lower retry attempts for idempotent calls. Also implement a 429 backoff response from Redwood so clients can react.

[10:25] Sofia Alvarez: On roadmap alignment, which upcoming Redwood features should we expect that impact cost and reliability?

[10:38] Maya Chen: For the next quarter: 1) improved continuous batching engine with dynamic windowing, 2) better quantization profiles in the catalog, and 3) rollout guardrails in Console for canary/A-B style deploys. Those map directly to cost and tail reduction.

[11:05] Derek Chu: Any ETA on the dynamic windowing?

[11:10] Arun Patel: Beta in 6 weeks, GA in ~12 weeks; we'll invite you to the pilot.

[11:22] Ravi Menon: Great. For the pilot, we want to run our sample workload end-to-end on your Dedicated pilot nodes. Can we schedule a benchmark with our dev keys?

[11:35] Maya Chen: Yes — action item: run a 2-hour benchmark with your sample prompts and traffic patterns, capture latency distributions and token cost. Arun will coordinate.

[11:50] Priya Iyer: Regarding security, our procurement asked for a data residency note — where is data stored for hosted vs Dedicated?

[12:02] Lila Gomez: Hosted data is stored in the region you select and we support EU/US/APAC regions. Dedicated and Private keep customer data within the customer's VPC or on-prem, depending on deployment. I'll include the residency table in the follow-up.

[12:32] Sofia Alvarez: Can we see the canary rollback policy in Console? We need to be able to flip back quickly if quality drops.

[12:45] Arun Patel: Console supports traffic split and automatic rollback based on error and quality thresholds tied to your eval set. We'll help you set the thresholds.

[13:10] Ravi Menon: A bit of spiral here, but what's the cost delta to run our low-latency route on a larger GPU with higher memory vs sharded smaller ones?

[13:25] Arun Patel: Larger GPUs reduce cross-shard overhead and can reduce per-token latency but may be slightly more expensive per-minute. For high QPS low-latency workloads, larger single-node configs often win on total cost of ownership because of fewer context-switches and better KV cache locality. We'll model both.

[14:00] Maya Chen: Okay let's capture concrete next steps — Lila, can you list what you'll send after the call?

[14:12] Lila Gomez: I'll send: 1) SOC2 and Dedicated KMS brief, 2) region/residency table, 3) linked log correlation spreadsheet for the July spike, 4) cost delta deck for Dedicated vs Hosted, and 5) link to the pilot sign-up form.

[14:40] Maya Chen: Arun you'll lead the bench plan?

[14:45] Arun Patel: Yes — I will coordinate the benchmark and produce the 2-hour runbook and expected outputs (latency p50/p95/p99, token counts per route, and cost per endpoint).

[15:00] Ravi Menon: I'll share the sample prompt set and a sanitized production trace. Derek will help with the trace extraction.

[15:15] Derek Chu: Yep, we'll get that over.

[15:22] Sofia Alvarez: Procurement wants an enterprise SLA amendment. Maya, can you loop in sales ops?

[15:30] Maya Chen: Absolutely — I'll escalate to Sales Ops and legal and share an initial term sheet.

[15:40] Priya Iyer: One more ask — can you provide an operational playbook for cache degradation that we can import into PagerDuty?

[15:50] Lila Gomez: We'll provide a runbook and a suggested alert set.

[16:00] Maya Chen: Great. Quick recap then: runbook and logs from Violet, benchmark plan, security docs, Dedicated sizing/cost deck, and SLA term sheet. Any blockers?

[16:15] Ravi Menon: None on our side — just timing sensitivity, want pilot in next 3 weeks.

[16:25] Maya Chen: We'll aim to kick the benchmark within 7–10 days and get the Dedicated cost delta by end of week after.

[16:40] Arun Patel: I'll propose two dedicated pool sizes (conservative and aggressive) and the expected monthly cost delta.

[16:52] Maya Chen: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up in an email with links to all artifacts. End call.

Note: Transcript has inline imperfections: e.g., Redwood product names sometimes transcribed as red wood, K V cache as KV cache or K V-cash, etc.
